title: Treasurer is mowed down over inflation
full_text:
Treasurer Jim Chalmers has been accused of “waving the white flag on inflation” while trying to dodge blame for the government’s high spending, with a fresh spike in prices reigniting fears of another brutal rate rise on Melbourne Cup day.
Those who yesterday joined a chorus of criticism against the treasurer included former Reserve Bank of Australia Philip Lowe, NSW Premier Chris Minns and even his namesake Jim Penman, the founder of the Jim’s Mowing business, who labelled Mr Chalmers “completely incompetent’’.
Mr Lowe launched a blistering attack on Labor and demanded it rein in spending after new data showed inflation had risen to 4 per cent in August, up from 3.5 per cent in July.
As it is above the bank’s target band of two to three per cent, economists have warned households could be hit with another interest rate hike as soon as November 3, going beyond the 15-year-high rates were pushed to on Tuesday.
But despite RBA governor Michele Bullock singling out “domestic capacity pressures” as part of the inflation problem – exacerbated by the Middle East war – Mr Chalmers held firm yesterday that government spending was not the problem.
“We can see in today’s inflation figures that the overwhelming reason why annual headline inflation has come up in August compared to July is because of the impact of higher global oil prices flowing through to oil prices in Australia,” he claimed.
“That’s not an opinion.
“It’s a fact.” But, his insistence is at odds with Dr Lowe, who made a rare intervention into the economic debate and called out government spending for keeping inflation high.
“Government spending has been adding to demand progressively over time, and that’s putting upward pressure on inflation,” he told a podcast.
He called on governments to prioritise running “sizeable surpluses”. Shadow treasurer Tim Wilson accused the government of “waving the white flag on inflation and surrendering to persistent inflation and more rate hikes”.
“Yesterday the Reserve Bank was forced to raise interest rates for the fourth time this year. Today the inflation data shows exactly why. Australia has a homegrown inflation problem, and it was baked in before a single bomb was dropped on Tehran”, he said.
Mr Chalmers denied he was at odds with Ms Bullock, claiming she had made clear that the Middle East war was putting “substantial upward pressure on inflation here and around the world”, when, in fact, she had stated the war was “in addition to’’ the main factor of domestic spending.
NSW Premier Chris Minns and Queensland Treasurer David Janetzki also weighed in yesterday.
In a clear reference to his federal government counterparts, Mr Minns said: “I think every government has a responsibility to do what it can to take demand out of the economy.” Mr Janetzki said “the federal treasurer has some responsibility here”. “Domestic capacity pressures, that’s what (Ms Bullock said). Jim Chalmers has responsibility for it,” he said.
And Mr Penman, the man behind the $1bn franchise giant Jim’s Group of mowing, cleaning and almost everything else, was among the most heavily-critical of Mr Chalmers and the government, slamming their economic credentials.
“He (Mr Chalmers) is completely incompetent, there’s nobody on the frontbench who has the slightest idea of how the world works,’’ Mr Penman, 74, said.
“I think we’re in trouble as a nation.
We’ve got a recklessly extravagant big borrowing government constantly doing things to push up prices in a stupid pursuit of green objectives without regard to cost that increases burden on businesses.’’ EDITORIAL PAGE 24 “Jim Chalmers is waving the white flag on inflation and surrendering to persistent inflation and more rate hikes.’’ Shadow Treasurer Tim Wilson
